name: What should homeowners know about ultra-luxury finish lead times?

mainEntity.name: Which luxury materials and products create the biggest schedule delays?
mainEntity.text: Which luxury materials and products create the biggest schedule delays?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ultra-luxury homes often depend on materials that are made to order, imported, or heavily customized. Those items can have much longer lead times than standard construction products, and they can affect the sequence of the entire project. Windows and doors may determine rough openings, cabinetry can affect plumbing and electrical layouts, and custom stone or millwork can control final finish timing. The builder should identify these items early and track them from the beginning of preconstruction. Homeowners should also ask what substitutions are acceptable if a product becomes unavailable. Waiting too long to order premium items is one of the most common reasons luxury projects slip. The safest strategy is to lock in important selections early and manage procurement as actively as the field work.
acceptedAnswer.description: The biggest lead-time risks are usually custom windows and doors, imported stone, specialty appliances, cabinetry, millwork, lighting, and bespoke hardware. These items often need to be ordered early because fabrication, shipping, and coordination can take weeks or months. Late ordering can delay other trades and push back completion.
